entries.1:1: Paul introduces himself as someone chosen and sent by Jesus, writing to believers in Ephesus who trust in Christ. It reminds the reader that ordinary Christians are included among God's holy people.
entries.1:2: Paul wishes his readers kindness and peace that come from God and Jesus. The reader can expect real grace and peace from God in daily life.
entries.1:3: God, the Father of Jesus, deserves our praise because he has blessed believers with every spiritual blessing through Christ. The reader can be thankful that these blessings are already theirs in him.
entries.1:4: God chose us to belong to Christ long ago so that we would live holy, blameless lives marked by love. The reader is called to live a clean and loving life because God set them apart for that.
entries.1:5: God planned in advance, out of his own good pleasure, to adopt believers as his own children through Jesus. The reader can know they are wanted and belong in God's family.
entries.1:6: All this is meant to bring praise to God's wonderful grace, which he poured out freely on us in his beloved Son. The reader's life can point to how generous God has been.
entries.1:7: Through Christ's death we are set free and our sins are forgiven, all because of God's overflowing grace. The reader can be sure their sins are truly forgiven, not earned but given.
entries.1:8: God gave this grace to us generously, along with deep wisdom and understanding. The reader can trust that God knows what he is doing and gives more than enough.
entries.1:9: God let us in on his hidden plan, which he had decided beforehand and intended to carry out. The reader can know that history is not random but follows God's purpose.
entries.1:10: When the right time comes, God will bring everything in heaven and earth together under Christ as the head. The reader can look forward to a day when everything is put right under Jesus.
entries.1:11: In Christ we receive an inheritance, because God marked us out beforehand and works everything according to his plan. The reader can be confident that their future is secure in God's hands.
entries.1:12: God's purpose is that we who hoped in Christ first would bring him praise. The reader's hope and life can be a way of honoring God.
entries.1:13: When you heard the true message of salvation and believed in Christ, you were marked with the Holy Spirit as God's own. The reader can know the Spirit in them is proof they belong to God.
entries.1:14: The Holy Spirit is a down payment on our inheritance, guaranteeing that God will fully redeem his people to his praise. The reader can be sure God will finish what he started.
entries.1:15: Paul had heard about the faith and love of these believers and mentions it as his reason for praying. The reader is encouraged that genuine faith and love get noticed and matter.
entries.1:16: Paul keeps thanking God for them and remembers them constantly in his prayers. The reader can see that praying thankfully for others is a normal part of following Jesus.
entries.1:17: Paul asks God to give them wisdom and insight so they can know him better. The reader can pray for a deeper, clearer knowledge of God himself.
entries.1:18: Paul prays that their hearts would be enlightened so they understand the hope God calls them to and the rich inheritance he gives his people. The reader can ask God to open their eyes to what they already have in him.
entries.1:19: Paul wants them to grasp how enormously powerful God's strength is toward those who believe. The reader can trust that the same power is at work for them.
entries.1:20: That power is the very strength God used to raise Christ from the dead and seat him at his right hand in heaven. The reader's faith rests on a God who defeats death itself.
entries.1:21: Christ is far above every ruler, authority, power, and name, both now and in the world to come. The reader can be confident no power outranks Jesus.
entries.1:22: God put everything under Christ's feet and made him head over everything for the church. The reader belongs to a body led by the one who rules over all.
entries.1:23: The church is Christ's body, filled and completed by him who fills everything. The reader is part of something that displays Christ himself to the world.
entries.2:1: Paul reminds readers that before God acted, they were spiritually dead because of their sins. It means your wrongdoing left you unable to give yourself spiritual life, so any life you have comes from God.
entries.2:2: In the past they followed the world's ways and the influence of an evil spiritual power that still drives people who resist God. It means the pull toward wrong is real and comes from outside you as well as inside.
entries.2:3: All people, including Paul's readers, once lived by their own selfish desires and deserved God's judgment. It means no one is naturally better than anyone else; everyone starts in the same guilty place.
entries.2:4: God, rich in mercy and great love, stepped in despite all that. It means God's kindness toward you is not because you deserved it but because of who he is.
entries.2:5: Even while people were spiritually dead in sin, God gave them life together with Christ, and this salvation comes as a gift. It means God acted first, before you could do anything to earn it.
entries.2:6: God raised believers with Christ and gave them a place with him in the heavenly realm. It means your standing with God is secure and honored, not something you have to climb toward.
entries.2:7: God did this so that in the ages to come he could show the full richness of his grace shown to us in Christ. It means God's kindness toward you is meant to be seen and praised forever.
entries.2:8: Salvation comes by God's grace through faith, and even that faith is not something you produce yourself; it is God's gift. It means you receive salvation rather than achieve it.
entries.2:9: It is not earned by works, so no one can boast about it. It means you have nothing to brag about before God, and no one else does either.
entries.2:10: God made us new in Christ Jesus to do good works that he had already prepared for us. It means good works are the result of God's work in you, not the price of your salvation.
entries.2:11: Paul asks Gentile believers to remember that they were once looked down on by those who were circumcised as a physical sign. It means remember where you came from and don't let labels divide you.
entries.2:12: At that time they had no Christ, no share in Israel's privileges, no part in God's covenant promises, no hope, and no God in the world. It means life without God is genuinely empty and hopeless.
entries.2:13: But now, in Christ Jesus, those who were far away have been brought near through his blood. It means Christ's death closed the distance between you and God.
entries.2:14: Christ himself is our peace; he made the two groups one and tore down the wall of hostility between them. It means peace with God and peace with others both come through him.
entries.2:15: By his death he set aside the law's rules that kept people divided, so that in himself he could create one new people out of the two. It means Christ removes the barriers that separate people from each other.
entries.2:16: Through the cross he reconciled both groups to God in one body, ending the hostility. It means the cross brings people together with God and with each other at the same time.
entries.2:17: Christ came and announced peace both to those far off and to those near. It means no one is too distant for his message of peace to reach.
entries.2:18: Through Christ, both groups can come to the Father by one Spirit. It means you have direct access to God, not through a special class or ritual.
entries.2:19: You are no longer outsiders or strangers but fellow citizens with God's people and members of his household. It means you truly belong to God's family.
entries.2:20: The church is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone. It means the whole structure depends on Christ to hold it together.
entries.2:21: In Christ the whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple for the Lord. It means God's presence lives among his people as they are built together.
entries.2:22: In Christ you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit. It means you are part of God's home, not just a visitor to it.
entries.3:1: Paul says he is in prison because of his work for Christ on behalf of non-Jewish people. It reminds the reader that serving God can cost something, but the purpose is still worth it.
entries.3:2: Paul reminds them that God gave him a special job of sharing grace with them. It means God's kindness toward you is not random; he deliberately reaches out to you.
entries.3:3: Paul says God revealed a hidden plan to him directly, which he already mentioned briefly. It means God does not keep his most important purposes secret from those he loves.
entries.3:4: Paul says that when they read his letter, they can see he understands this hidden plan about Christ. It means reading Scripture carefully helps you grasp what God is doing.
entries.3:5: This plan was not made known to earlier generations, but now God has revealed it to his apostles and prophets by the Spirit. It means you live in a time when God's purposes are clearer than ever before.
entries.3:6: The hidden plan is that non-Jewish people share equally in God's family, the same body, and the same hope in Christ through the good news. It means you belong fully, with no second-class place, if you are in Christ.
entries.3:7: Paul became a servant of this good news by God's grace and power working in him. It means God equips ordinary people with his strength to do work that matters.
entries.3:8: Paul calls himself the least of all God's people, yet he was given the task of telling non-Jews about Christ's endless riches. It means God can use anyone, even someone who feels small, to share something priceless.
entries.3:9: Paul's job is to help everyone see this plan that God, the maker of all things, kept hidden for ages. It means God has been working toward this all along, and now it is out in the open.
entries.3:10: Through the church, God now shows his rich wisdom to the spiritual powers in the heavenly places. It means the church is not just a gathering; it displays God's wisdom to unseen realms.
entries.3:11: This plan comes from God's eternal purpose, which he carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord. It means God's plan for you is not an afterthought; it was always his intention.
entries.3:12: Through Christ we can come close to God with confidence, by trusting him. It means you do not have to be afraid to approach God; faith in Jesus gives you open access.
entries.3:13: Paul asks them not to be discouraged by his troubles, because those troubles serve their glory. It means hard things done for others can bring real benefit, so don't lose heart.
entries.3:14: Because of all this, Paul kneels in prayer to the Father. It means prayer is the natural response to seeing what God is doing.
entries.3:15: Every family in heaven and on earth gets its name from the Father. It means all belonging ultimately comes from God, who is the source of every family.
entries.3:16: Paul prays that God, out of his rich glory, will make them strong inwardly through his Spirit. It means real strength is inside you, given by God, not just outward.
entries.3:17: He prays that Christ will make his home in their hearts through faith, and that they will be rooted and grounded in love. It means faith lets Christ settle in deeply, and love becomes your foundation.
entries.3:18: Paul prays they will have power, together with all God's people, to grasp how wide, long, high, and deep God's love is. It means understanding God's love takes strength and is best done alongside other believers.
entries.3:19: He prays they will know Christ's love, which is beyond full knowledge, so they can be filled to God's own fullness. It means God's love is bigger than you can fully understand, yet knowing it makes you complete.
entries.3:20: God can do more than you would even think to ask. Your imagination is the smaller limit.
entries.3:21: Paul ends by giving glory to God in the church and in Christ Jesus for all generations forever. It means the church's purpose is to honor God, and that honor never ends.
entries.4:1: Paul, writing as a prisoner, urges readers to live in a way that matches the calling God gave them. Your everyday life should reflect what God has called you to be.
entries.4:2: Be humble, gentle, and patient, bearing with one another's faults because you love them. Treat the people around you with quiet kindness even when it's hard.
entries.4:3: Work hard to stay united in peace, keeping the harmony the Spirit gives. Don't let small conflicts break the bond between you and others.
entries.4:4: There is one body of believers and one Spirit, just as God gave you one shared hope. Remember you belong to one family with a common future.
entries.4:5: There is one Lord, one faith, and one baptism. What unites believers is far greater than what divides them.
entries.4:6: There is one God and Father over everyone, working through all and living in all. You are never outside his care or presence.
entries.4:7: Each person receives grace from Christ in the measure he chooses to give. Don't compare your gifts with others; use what you've been given.
entries.4:8: Paul quotes Scripture to say Christ ascended in triumph and gave gifts to people. His victory is the reason you receive anything good.
entries.4:9: The one who went up is the same one who first came down to the lowest place. Christ didn't stay distant; he came all the way down to where we are.
entries.4:10: The one who came down is the same one who went up above all the heavens, so he could fill everything. Christ is over all things and completes them.
entries.4:11: Christ gave different roles to different people: apostles, prophets, evangelists, and pastors and teachers. Not everyone has the same job, and that's by design.
entries.4:12: These roles exist to equip believers for service and to build up the church. Leaders are there to help ordinary believers do the work, not to do it all themselves.
entries.4:13: This equipping continues until we all share one faith, know God's Son deeply, and grow to full maturity in Christ. Spiritual growth is a lifelong process, not a quick fix.
entries.4:14: Maturity keeps us from being tossed around by every new teaching and tricked by clever deceivers. Learn to recognize error so you aren't easily led astray.
entries.4:15: Speak the truth in love and grow up into Christ, who is the head of the church. Truth without love wounds, and love without truth misleads; you need both.
entries.4:16: The whole body, joined and held together, grows as each part does its work in love. Your contribution matters; the church grows when everyone plays their part.
entries.4:17: Paul insists that believers must stop living the way people do when they don't know God, chasing things that lead nowhere. Your new life should look different from your old one.
entries.4:18: Their minds are darkened and cut off from God's life because of ignorance and hard hearts. A hard heart keeps you from understanding what God offers.
entries.4:19: Having lost sensitivity, they gave themselves over to greed and impurity. Repeatedly ignoring your conscience makes it harder to hear it.
entries.4:20: This is not what you learned when you were taught about Christ. Your faith should shape your life in a completely different direction.
entries.4:21: You heard him and were taught in him, since the truth is found in Jesus. What you believe about Jesus should come from what he actually taught.
entries.4:22: Set aside your old self, corrupted by deceitful desires. Your former way of living has to be deliberately left behind.
entries.4:23: Be renewed in the way you think. Change starts in your mind; let God reshape how you see things.
entries.4:24: Put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness. Live as the new person God has made you to be.
entries.4:25: Stop lying and tell the truth to your neighbor, because you belong to each other. Honesty matters because we're connected as one body.
entries.4:26: It's possible to be angry without sinning, but don't let anger linger overnight. Deal with anger quickly before it takes root.
entries.4:27: Don't give the devil an opening. Unresolved anger and sin give the enemy room to work in your life.
entries.4:28: Thieves should stop stealing and work honestly so they can help those in need. Honest work isn't just for yourself; it's so you can be generous.
entries.4:29: Don't let harmful words come out of your mouth; say only what builds others up and benefits those who hear. Your words should help, not hurt.
entries.4:30: Don't grieve God's Holy Spirit, who sealed you for the day of redemption. Your choices matter to God; he is personally involved in your life.
entries.4:31: Get rid of bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, slander, and every kind of malice. These attitudes poison relationships and have no place in a believer's life.
entries.4:32: Be kind and forgive, because you were forgiven first. The reason comes before the rule.
entries.5:1: God loves you like a father loves his children, so you should want to act like him. Let that be your aim in everyday life.
entries.5:2: Live a life of love, following Christ's example, who loved you and gave himself for you as a gift to God. Love that gives itself away pleases God.
entries.5:3: Sexual sin, any kind of impurity, and greed should not even be talked about among you, because that doesn't fit people who belong to God.
entries.5:4: Don't use dirty talk, silly joking, or crude humor; instead, say things that give thanks and build others up.
entries.5:5: You can be sure that anyone who lives in sexual sin, impurity, greed, or idolatry has no share in the kingdom of Christ and God.
entries.5:6: Don't let anyone fool you with empty words; God's judgment comes on people who live in disobedience to him.
entries.5:7: Don't join in with people who live like that.
entries.5:8: You used to live in darkness, but now you are light because of the Lord, so live like people who belong to the light.
entries.5:9: The fruit of light shows up in doing what is right, good, and true.
entries.5:10: Learn by experience what pleases the Lord, and make that your aim.
entries.5:11: Don't take part in the dark things people do that produce nothing good; instead, expose them for what they are.
entries.5:12: The things those people do in secret are so shameful that it's embarrassing even to mention them.
entries.5:13: But when light shines on something, its true nature is exposed and made visible.
entries.5:14: That's why it says: wake up, you who are asleep, rise from among the dead, and Christ will shine on you.
entries.5:15: Be careful how you live; don't live like a fool, but like someone wise.
entries.5:16: Make the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil.
entries.5:17: So don't be foolish; instead, understand what the Lord wants.
entries.5:18: Don't get drunk on wine, which leads to ruin; instead, be filled with the Spirit.
entries.5:19: Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making music to the Lord in your heart.
entries.5:20: Always give thanks for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
entries.5:21: Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.
entries.5:22: Wives, submit to your husbands as you would to the Lord.
entries.5:23: The husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church, his body, of which he is the Savior.
entries.5:24: Just as the church submits to Christ, so wives should submit to their husbands in everything.
entries.5:25: Husbands, love your wives just as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it.
entries.5:26: Christ gave himself to make the church holy, cleansing it by the washing of water through the word.
entries.5:27: He did this to present the church to himself in splendor, without any spot or wrinkle or anything like that, but holy and without blame.
entries.5:28: In the same way, husbands should love their wives as they love their own bodies; a man who loves his wife loves himself.
entries.5:29: No one ever hated his own body; instead, he feeds and cares for it, just as Christ cares for the church.
entries.5:30: We are members of Christ's body.
entries.5:31: That's why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
entries.5:32: This is a profound mystery, and I'm saying it refers to Christ and the church.
entries.5:33: Each of you husbands must love his wife as he loves himself, and each wife must respect her husband.
entries.6:1: Children should obey their parents because this is the right thing to do in following the Lord. If you are a child, this means listening to your mom and dad as part of your faith.
entries.6:2: Honoring your father and mother means treating them with real respect, and this is the first command that comes with a promise attached. For you, it means showing your parents genuine honor, not just going through the motions.
entries.6:3: The promise is that things will go well for you and you will live long on the earth. This tells you that God attaches a real blessing to how you treat your parents.
entries.6:4: Fathers are told not to provoke their children to anger but to raise them with training and instruction that honors the Lord. If you are a parent, this means correcting and teaching your kids without harshness that stirs up resentment.
entries.6:5: Servants are told to obey their earthly masters with respect and sincerity, as if they were serving Christ. For you, it means doing your work wholeheartedly because ultimately you are serving the Lord, not just a boss.
entries.6:6: Don't work hard only when the boss is watching to impress people; work sincerely as servants of Christ doing what God wants. For you, it means your effort should be honest and consistent whether or not anyone is watching.
entries.6:7: Do your work willingly, as though you were doing it for the Lord rather than for people. For you, this means your attitude toward your job changes when you see it as service to God.
entries.6:8: God will reward every good thing anyone does, whether they are a servant or free. For you, this means no good work goes unnoticed by God, regardless of your status or position.
entries.6:9: Masters are told to treat their servants the same way, without threats, knowing that both they and their servants have the same Master in heaven who shows no favoritism. If you have authority over others, this means treating them fairly and remembering God judges you by the same standard.
entries.6:10: Be strong, but not in your own strength—be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. For you, this means drawing your strength from God rather than relying on yourself.
entries.6:11: Put on the full armor God provides so you can stand firm against the devil's schemes. For you, this means using what God gives you to resist temptation and deception.
entries.6:12: Our real struggle is not against people but against spiritual forces of evil and darkness. For you, this means remembering that the people who oppose you are not the true enemy.
entries.6:13: So take up all of God's armor so you can stand firm when evil days come and, after doing everything, still be standing. For you, this means being prepared ahead of time so you don't collapse when hard times hit.
entries.6:14: Stand firm with truth like a belt around your waist and righteousness like a breastplate protecting your heart. For you, this means letting honesty and right living guard you.
entries.6:15: Be ready to move with the good news of peace, like shoes on your feet. For you, this means being prepared to share and live out the peace the gospel brings wherever you go.
entries.6:16: Above all, use faith as a shield to block all the flaming arrows of the evil one. For you, this means trusting God is what stops the devil's attacks from doing damage.
entries.6:17: Take salvation as your helmet and the word of God as the sword the Spirit gives you. For you, this means letting your security in God protect your mind and using Scripture to face spiritual battles.
entries.6:18: Pray at all times in the Spirit with every kind of request, staying alert and persistent, praying for all God's people. For you, this means prayer should be constant and include others, not just yourself.
entries.6:19: Paul asks them to pray that he will be given the right words to boldly make the gospel clear. For you, this means praying for those who share the message, that they would speak clearly and without fear.
entries.6:20: Paul is an ambassador for the gospel even while in chains, and he asks for boldness to say what he should. For you, this means circumstances don't excuse you from speaking the truth courageously.
entries.6:21: Tychicus, a trusted and beloved brother, will tell them all the news about Paul. For you, this means good leaders keep people informed and send trustworthy people to do it.
entries.6:22: Paul sent Tychicus so they would know how things are and so their hearts would be comforted. For you, this means sharing news and encouragement is a real way to care for others.
entries.6:23: Paul prays that God the Father and Jesus Christ will give the believers peace, love, and faith. For you, this means peace and love are gifts that come from God, not things you manufacture alone.
entries.6:24: Paul ends by asking that grace be with everyone who truly loves Jesus Christ. For you, this means genuine love for Jesus is the mark of those who receive God's grace.
